newsitem.title: USA: ITT profits narrowly beat Wall Street forecast.
newsitem.headline: ITT profits narrowly beat Wall Street forecast.

text.p: ITT Corp., fighting a hostile takeover attempt by rival Hilton Hotels Corp., Tuesday reported first-quarter profits that slightly exceeded Wall Street expectations.
Net income hit $80 million, or 68 cents a share, a fourfold increase from $20 million, or 17 cents per share, in the first quarter of 1996.

The 1997 results, however, included a number of one-time items, including an after-tax gain of $106 million on the sale of ITT's stake in French telecommunications conglomerate Alcatel Alsthom. The latest quarter also included an after-tax charge of $12 million to defend against Hilton's January bid -- as well as income from assets the New York-based company plans to sell as part of its takeover defence.
Beverly Hills, Calif.-based Hilton's has bid $6.5 billion, or $55 a share for ITT.
Excluding both the assets for sale and the one-time items, ITT said its operating earnings rose to $32 million, or 27 cents a share, from $17 million, or 15 cents a share in the year-ago period.
Revenues rose to $1.41 billion from $1.33 billion.

"We continue to focus on growing our core lodging and gaming businesses for the benefit of ITT shareholders," company Chairman Rand Araskog said in a statement. "Both of these businesses are operationally strong with Sheraton (hotels) registering its first quarter ever and Caesars World (casinos) posting a solid performance despite major construction projects at its two largest properties."

In addition to takeover defence costs and the Alcatel Alsthom gain, ITT's one-time item includes an after-tax charge of $33 million for trimming the size of the company's headquarters and headquarters staff.
The company also recorded an after-tax loss of $13 million at The Desert Inn in Las Vegas and ITT's riverboat casino in Tunica, Miss., both of which ITT plans to sell.
The company said earnings at its ITT Sheraton unit rose 30 percent to $117 million before interest, taxes, depreciation and other items.

Underlying earnings in its gambling operations, excluding The Desert Inn and the riverboat casino, fell to $65 million from $71 million in 1996. The company attributed the decline primarily to the construction at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas, which is expected to be completed by year-end.
